pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #8
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Overgrazing continuously

2. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Ice melting to water

3. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

4. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 0 °C

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Light.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.

6. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. newton (N)
   C. watt (W)
   D. pascal (Pa)

7. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

8. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

9. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Properties of Matter? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Properties of Matter.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Matter.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Properties of Matter.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Properties of Matter.

11. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Nitrogen gas only

12. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Tertiary consumers
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Producers

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Heat? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Heat.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Heat.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Heat.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Heat.

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water Conservation? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water Conservation.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water Conservation.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water Conservation.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Water Conservation.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
15. In three clear sentences, explain Water Conservation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Heat and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Properties of Matter and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Water Conservation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Heat and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Properties of Matter and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Water Conservation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
